podcast.body: David Bowie worked on this album throughout 2000 and 2001, intending it to feature new versions of his earliest songs alongside three new tracks, with a proposed release date in 2002. Although the album was completed and ready for release, it was shelved, with the re-recordings of his early 1960s material remaining officially unreleased. "Through 2000 and 2001, Bowie worked on an album called Toy. We were told it would feature some new versions of some of his earliest songs, along with three new tracks. Release date? Sometime in 2002. But then, nothing. The album is finished. It's ready to be released, but it is for some reason still on the shelf."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Started in 2000, this album was intended to feature re-recordings of obscure songs from Bowie's early career, with production and artwork fully completed. Bowie himself blogged about the project, which ultimately was never released due to a rumored disagreement with Virgin Records, who were reportedly not interested in an album featuring songs for which they didn't own the rights. "Production was completed, art work was finished, and Bowie even blogged about everything himself. He called the record, toy."
